counterfactual_missing_items: R2 omits the dextrocardia/situs-inversus anatomy that explains the rightsided cardiac impulse, left hepatic dullness, and diagnostic ECG pattern
R4 omits the acute myocardial infarction evidence: troponin elevation, ST-segment elevations, and RCA occlusion
R1 explains only the left hepatic dullness and does not account for troponin, ST elevations, coronary angiography, or dextrocardia
decisive_items: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
response.rationale: C1 is the only supplied candidate that integrates the acute RCA-occlusion myocardial infarction with the mirrored cardiac anatomy shown by echo and ECG. R2 is the best acute-MI component but misses dextrocardia/situs inversus; R4 captures only the anatomy; R1 has a weak through a single abdominal finding.

rejected.why: Anatomically supported but omits the acute MI evidence, especially troponin, ST elevations, and RCA occlusion.
Cor pulmonale is not supported by the coronary angiography, troponin, and ST-elevation MI pattern, and the left hepatic dullness is better explained by situs inversus.
